hooks.text: Winnie-the-Pooh was bought for twenty dollars at a Canadian train stop.
Did you know a real World War I bear inspired Winnie-the-Pooh?
A black bear cub was purchased for twenty dollars in 1914.

title: The Real Bear Behind Winnie-the-Pooh
description: Discover the true story of Winnipeg, the real black bear cub bought by a Canadian veterinarian who inspired Winnie-the-Pooh.

beats.text: Winnie-the-Pooh was bought for twenty dollars at a Canadian train stop.
beats.visual: American black bear cub sitting near a railway station in White River, Ontario, 1914

beats.text: In August 1914, Canadian veterinarian Lieutenant Harry [Colebourn](/kˈOlbˈɔɹn/) purchased an orphaned black bear cub.
beats.visual: Lieutenant Harry Colebourn with black bear cub Winnipeg, 1914

beats.text: He named her Winnipeg after his hometown, and she became the official mascot of the Canadian Army Veterinary Corps.
beats.visual: Canadian Army Veterinary Corps troops with mascot bear at military camp

beats.text: The bear sailed across the Atlantic aboard the S.S. Manitou in October 1914 with troops heading to England.
beats.visual: Steamship S.S. Manitou at sea carrying troops, 1914

beats.text: After living with the troops at Salisbury Plain, [Colebourn](/kˈOlbˈɔɹn/) left Winnie safely at the London Zoo.
beats.visual: London Zoo historic bear enclosure in the early twentieth century

beats.text: There, a young boy named Christopher Robin [Milne](/mˈɪln/) fell in love with the gentle bear.
beats.visual: Young Christopher Robin Milne visiting the London Zoo

beats.text: He renamed his own teddy bear in her honor, directly inspiring Winnie-the-Pooh.
beats.visual: Original Winnie-the-Pooh teddy bear at the New York Public Library
queries: Winnie the Pooh original teddy bear

better_than_last: This episode applies a tight narrative structure focused on a surprising historical origin for a globally famous subject.
